title: State-of-controls ledger record
description: One line of company-profile/<company_id>/soc/main.jsonl. The ledger is append-only: a record is never edited, it is superseded by appending a new record whose 'supersedes' names the old id. Five record kinds share a base and follow NIST OSCAL 1.1.3 assessment-results vocabulary: control (implemented-requirement), observation (evidence collected by a method), finding (a gap against a control, SARIF-shaped), risk (risk register entry) and incident (a security event with regulator reporting clocks)

examples.title: Software Bill of Materials for critical systems
examples.statement: An SBOM is generated for every production image of the trading platform on each release and stored under applications/<app_id>/images
examples.notes: SBOM exists for the API image but not for the batch-settlement image

examples.title: CI pipeline generates SBOM for trading-api but not batch-settlement
examples.description: The GitHub Actions workflow release.yml runs cyclonedx-npm on the trading-api image; the batch-settlement Dockerfile has no SBOM step

examples.title: batch-settlement image ships lodash 4.17.20 with CVE-2021-23337
examples.description: The batch-settlement production image contains lodash 4.17.20, vulnerable to command injection via template. No SBOM was generated so the package was not tracked

examples.title: Untracked third-party components in settlement pipeline
examples.statement: Because no SBOM exists for the batch-settlement image, a vulnerable dependency may reach production undetected and disrupt T+1 settlement

mitigations.description: Add cyclonedx step to the batch-settlement release job and gate on grype critical/high

examples.title: Exploitation attempt against lodash template in batch-settlement
examples.description: WAF logs show crafted template payloads hitting the settlement report endpoint from a single IP; no evidence of successful execution
examples.rootCause: Vulnerable lodash version not detected because the image had no SBOM and no scan gate

timeline.note: Endpoint disabled and source IP blocked at the perimeter

recordId.description: Any ledger record id: an instrument-qualified control id ('<instrumentId>:<controlId>') for controls, or a prefixed ULID (obs_, fnd_, rsk_, inc_) for generated records. The two forms cannot overlap because a controlId never contains ':'

qualifiedControlId.description: Ledger identity of a control: '<instrumentId>:<controlId>', e.g. 'sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5'. The prefix is frameworkRefs[0].instrument (a vocab/instruments id) and the suffix frameworkRefs[0].controlId, so numbered clauses from different instruments (PCI DSS '1.2.1', an RBI clause '1.2.1', CIS '1.2') never collide in one ledger. The instrument alternation in the pattern must equal the vocab/instruments enum; regenerate it when the vocab changes

base.description: Fields every ledger record carries. kind, id and supersedes are narrowed by each record kind. Records produced by a harness (claude-code, opencode) must carry provenance.sessionId, workflow and agent because cost_of_audit and the incident KPIs join the ledger on them (AGENTS.md section 4)

kind.description: Record discriminator; selects which branch of this schema applies

id.description: Stable identity of the record across supersessions: '<instrumentId>:<controlId>' for controls, a prefixed ULID otherwise

recordedAt.description: When this line was appended to the ledger; monotonically non-decreasing within main.jsonl

companyId.description: Company the ledger belongs to; must equal the <company_id> directory name

supersedes.description: id of the earlier record of the same kind that this record replaces. For controls and findings it equals this record's own id (same identity, newer state); for observations it points at the observation being refreshed. Each kind narrows it to its own id shape, so a finding can never supersede an observation

tags.description: Free-form lowercase labels for filtering, e.g. 'supply-chain', 'pci:req6'

provenance.description: Who and which run appended the record; KPIs are attributed through it. sessionId, workflow and agent are required when harness is claude-code or opencode; set runId from MAXWELL_RUN_ID whenever a run id exists

owner.description: Accountable party: a full actor object, or simply the human's email (common owner)

controlIds.description: Instrument-qualified control ids ('<instrumentId>:<controlId>') the record relates to; each must exist as a control record in this ledger

regulatoryRefs.description: Clauses cited; prefer the most specific Indian instrument first, global mappings after

evidence.description: Evidence supporting the record, as workspace files, URLs, tickets or tool outputs

control.description: OSCAL implemented-requirement: the company's current implementation state of one framework control

id.description: '<instrumentId>:<controlId>' built from frameworkRefs[0], e.g. 'sebi-cscrf-2024:GV.SC.S5'; a newer control record with the same id supersedes the older one

frameworkRefs.description: The instrument clause this control implements first (its instrument and controlId form this record's id), then equivalent clauses in other instruments

title.description: Control heading as in the regulator catalog

statement.description: How the company implements the control, in the company's own terms (OSCAL implemented-requirement statement)

category.description: Framework category the control sits in, e.g. NIST CSF 'PR.AA', CSCRF 'GV.SC'

implementationStatus.description: OSCAL implementation-status of the control today

effectiveness.description: Outcome of the last assessment of the control's operation; 'not-tested' until an observation exists

applicableAssets.description: Assets the control is expected to cover; empty or omitted means company-wide

parameters.description: OSCAL set-parameter values chosen by the company, e.g. sbomFormat=cyclonedx-1.6, passwordMinLength=14

lastAssessedAt.description: When the most recent observation against this control was collected

nextDueAt.description: When the control must next be re-assessed, from the catalog cadence

notes.description: Assessor remarks, gaps and compensating controls

observation.description: OSCAL observation: what a workflow, interview or document review saw about one or more controls, with the evidence it produced

title.description: One-line statement of what was observed

description.description: What was examined, what was seen and why it matters for the listed controls

methods.description: OSCAL observation methods: the Maxwell workflow that produced it, or 'manual', 'interview', 'document-review' for human collection. The utility entry points (validate, kpis, seed-company, status) are not observation methods

collectedAt.description: When the evidence was collected from the subject

expiresAt.description: When the observation should no longer be relied on and the control needs re-probing

result.description: Assessment outcome for the listed controls: satisfied, not-satisfied, partial, not-applicable, or inconclusive when access or evidence was insufficient

toolOutput.description: Raw tool output the observation was derived from, stored in the session raw directory as kpis/data/raw/sessions/<sessionId>/<workflow>.<format>.export.json (the only raw-output file name layout.json sanctions there)

format.description: Output format: SARIF 2.1.0, OCSF 1.x events, or plain text

path.description: Workspace path of the stored output; must be kpis/data/raw/sessions/<sessionId>/<name>.export.json so validate-layout accepts it, e.g. 'kpis/data/raw/sessions/8f3b1c2a-4d5e-4f60-9a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/probe-cicd-env.sarif.export.json'

sha256.description: Digest of the stored output for tamper evidence

finding.description: OSCAL finding shaped like a SARIF result: a gap against one or more controls with severity, SLA and lifecycle status

title.description: One-line statement of the gap, naming the asset and the weakness

description.description: Detail: what was found, how it was confirmed, impact and suggested fix

severity.description: Canonical severity: derive from cvss when present, else copy the regulator catalog control's defaultSeverity (catalog/regulator-catalog $defs/control.defaultSeverity) for the most specific instrument cited; never estimate it

confidence.description: How sure the source is that the finding is real

target.description: The asset the finding is about; use type 'company' for company-wide gaps. Part of the fingerprint and the unit report and remediation workflows act on

location.description: SARIF physicalLocation: where in the target the finding sits

path.description: SARIF artifactLocation.uri: path relative to the repo root or image filesystem (uriBaseId semantics), never absolute and never traversing upwards

endLine.description: SARIF region.endLine, 1-based, not less than startLine

url.description: Deep link to the location in the SCM or console

fingerprint.description: sha256 over (source.ruleId, target, location.path, normalised message) with SARIF partialFingerprints semantics: stable across runs so re-runs supersede rather than duplicate

source.description: Where the finding came from. sarif sources must name the tool and rule; ocsf sources must name the OCSF class

kind.description: sarif for static or SCA tools, ocsf for security event feeds, runtime-probe for Maxwell live probes, agent-analysis for gaps an agent found by reading code, IaC, charts or policies without a scanner (probe-iac, probe-app-chart, probe-sdlc, refresh-vendor-ctx), manual for humans

ruleId.description: SARIF rule id or OCSF finding type id as emitted by the tool

ocsfClassUid.description: OCSF Findings category class: 2002 Vulnerability, 2003 Compliance, 2004 Detection, 2005 Incident, 2006 Data Security, 2007 Application Security Posture

cvss.description: CVSS scoring when the finding is a vulnerability. The vector shape is common cvssVector (shared with cve/record); the version must agree with the vector prefix

version.description: CVSS specification version of the vector

vector.description: Full vector string beginning with 'CVSS:3.0/', 'CVSS:3.1/' or 'CVSS:4.0/'; CVSS 4.0 supplemental metrics such as U:Clear, U:Green, U:Amber and U:Red are allowed

score.description: Base score 0.0-10.0 (same field name as cve/record cvss.score)

cveIds.description: CVE identifiers the finding corresponds to

status.description: Lifecycle status. risk-accepted, false-positive and duplicate require statusReason; resolved, risk-accepted, false-positive and duplicate require resolvedAt

statusReason.description: Why the status is what it is; required when status is risk-accepted, false-positive or duplicate

slaDueAt.description: firstSeenAt plus slaBasis.days; computed from the SLA table, never guessed

slaBasis.description: The SLA-table row (instrument, topic, severity) that set slaDueAt

instrument.description: Instrument whose clause set the deadline

controlId.description: Clause id within the instrument, when numbered

severity.description: Severity column of the SLA-table row matched: a canonical severity, or 'any' when the clause does not distinguish severities

days.description: Remediation days granted, copied from the row

suggestionIds.description: Code suggestions proposed to fix the finding

firstSeenAt.description: When the fingerprint was first observed; preserved across supersessions

lastSeenAt.description: When the fingerprint was most recently observed

resolvedAt.description: When status moved to resolved, risk-accepted, false-positive or duplicate; required for those statuses

risk.description: Risk-register entry: a potential loss event tied to findings, controls and threats, with likelihood and impact ratings

statement.description: Risk statement in the form 'Because <condition>, <event> may occur, causing <consequence>'

description.description: Context, affected processes and analysis behind the ratings

severity.description: Overall rating derived from likelihood and impact

likelihood.description: Probability the event occurs within a year

impact.description: Consequence if the event occurs, on customers, market integrity and the company

status.description: Lifecycle status; accepted and deviation-approved require acceptedBy and acceptedUntil

threatIds.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique ids (T1195.002) or ATLAS ids (AML.T0010) describing the threat

mitigations.description: Planned or running treatments, each optionally tracked as an initiative

description.description: What will be done to reduce likelihood or impact

deadline.description: Date by which the risk must be closed or formally accepted

acceptedBy.description: Who accepted the risk; required when status is accepted or deviation-approved

acceptedUntil.description: Expiry of the acceptance, after which the risk reopens; required when status is accepted or deviation-approved

incident.description: Security incident with response timestamps and regulator reporting clocks (CERT-In and RBI 6 hours, DPDP and NYDFS 72 hours). category and affectedDataClassifications decide which clocks apply; each regulatorReportRef names the instrument that set its deadline

description.description: What happened, what was affected and current understanding

status.description: Lifecycle status; contained and later statuses require containedAt, recovered and closed require resolvedAt

category.description: Incident type, mirroring the CERT-In Directions 2022 Annex I reportable incident types (SEBI CSCRF requires the same classification); 'other' only when no listed type fits

dedupKey.description: PagerDuty dedup_key (incident_key) of the incident, stored verbatim so it joins kpi/pagerduty-export incident_key by string equality (1-255 characters, the PagerDuty limit). Incidents Maxwell raises use the single format defined in kpi/pagerduty-export $defs/maxwellIncidentKey, 'maxwell:<controlId lower-cased>:<assetId>:<first 16 hex of the finding fingerprint>', which is enforced here for any key starting with 'maxwell:'; incidents ingested from PagerDuty, a SIEM or reported by a human keep whatever key the source set

detectedAt.description: When the incident was noticed; regulator clocks start here

containedAt.description: When the attacker's ability to cause further harm was removed; required once status is contained or later

resolvedAt.description: When services were fully restored and the incident closed; required when status is recovered or closed

regulatorReportRefs.description: One entry per regulator that must be notified, with the instrument that set the deadline clock and the submission reference

regulator.description: Supervisory authority receiving the report; standards bodies never receive incident reports

instrument.description: Instrument whose clause sets the reporting clock, e.g. cert-in-directions-2022 for the 6-hour CERT-In report

slaTopic.description: SLA-table topic of the row that set deadlineHours (incident-reporting, breach-notification, customer-notification)

deadlineHours.description: Hours from detectedAt within which the report is due, copied from the SLA table: 6 for CERT-In and RBI, 72 for DPDP and NYDFS

reference.description: Acknowledgement or ticket number returned by the regulator; required once submittedAt is set

submittedAt.description: When the report was submitted; absent while still pending

affectedDataClassifications.description: Classes of data touched by the incident; pii or spdi start the DPDP 72-hour clock, cardholder triggers PCI DSS notification

rootCause.description: Root cause once known, from the postmortem

pagerdutyId.description: PagerDuty incident id (the P... or Q... alphanumeric key), same shape as kpi/pagerduty-export
